evidence.excerpt: The equivalent series inductance (ESL) of the DC-link capacitor bank in a pulse-width-modulated inverter drive is often overlooked in EMC pre-compliance analysis yet contributes measurably to conducted emissions above 5 MHz. This study quantifies the effect by replacing a standard electrolytic capacitor bank (ESL ≈ 45 nH) with a film capacitor arrangement (ESL ≈ 8 nH) in a 4 kW test drive and recording the full conducted emission spectrum from 150 kHz to 30 MHz under identical load conditions. Peak differential-mode emissions between 10 MHz and 30 MHz were reduced by 6–11 dB with the lower-ESL bank. Impedance spectroscopy measurements confirmed the resonance shift from 9.2 MHz to above 30 MHz. A circuit-level simulation model incorporating measured parasitic parameters reproduced the spectral features within ±2 dB. The findings are directly applicable to PCB layout guidelines for compact drive modules targeting IEC 61800-3 Category C2 limits.
